questions.stem:
The following table shows the mean weight, $y\text{ kg}$, of children who are $x$ years old.

| **Age ($x$ years)** | $1.25$ | $2.25$ | $3.5$ | $4.4$ | $5.85$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Weight ($y$ kg)** | $10$ | $13$ | $14$ | $17$ | $19$ |

The relationship between the variables is modelled by the regression line with equation $y = ax + b$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(i) Find the value of $a$ and of $b$.

(ii) Write down the correlation coefficient.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use your equation to estimate the mean weight of a child that is $1.95$ years old.
parts.markscheme:
correct substitution into their equation ***(A1)***

eg $1.92 \times 1.95 + 7.98$

$11.7205$

$11.7$ (kg) ***A1*** ***N2***

questions.stem:
The following diagram shows quadrilateral ABCD.

**diagram not to scale**

![Quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal DB: AB = 11, BC = 6, angle BAD = 59°, angle ADB = 100° and angle CBD = 82°.](content/papers/img/2018-may-p2-tz2-q2.png)

$\text{AB} = 11\text{ cm}$, $\text{BC} = 6\text{ cm}$, $\text{B}\hat{\text{A}}\text{D} = 59^\circ$, $\text{A}\hat{\text{D}}\text{B} = 100^\circ$, and $\text{C}\hat{\text{B}}\text{D} = 82^\circ$

parts.label: a
parts.markscheme:
evidence of choosing sine rule ***(M1)***

eg $\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = \dfrac{b}{\sin B} = \dfrac{c}{\sin C}$

correct substitution ***(A1)***

eg $\dfrac{\text{DB}}{\sin 59^\circ} = \dfrac{11}{\sin 100^\circ}$

$9.57429$

$\text{DB} = 9.57$ (cm) ***A1*** ***N2***

parts.label: b
parts.markscheme:
evidence of choosing cosine rule ***(M1)***

eg $a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos(A)$, $\text{DC}^2 = \text{DB}^2 + \text{BC}^2 - 2\text{DB} \times \text{BC} \times \cos(\text{D}\hat{\text{B}}\text{C})$

correct substitution into RHS ***(A1)***

eg $9.57^2 + 6^2 - 2 \times 9.57 \times 6 \times \cos 82^\circ$, $111.677$

$10.5677$

$\text{DC} = 10.6$ (cm) ***A1*** ***N2***

questions.stem:
At an amusement park, a Ferris wheel with diameter $111$ metres rotates at a constant speed. The bottom of the wheel is $k$ metres above the ground. A seat starts at the bottom of the wheel.

**diagram not to scale**

![A Ferris wheel of diameter 111 on supports; the bottom of the wheel is k above the ground and it rotates anticlockwise.](content/papers/img/2018-may-p2-tz2-q6.png)

The wheel completes one revolution in $16$ minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: After $8$ minutes, the seat is $117\text{ m}$ above the ground. Find $k$.
parts.markscheme:
valid approach to find $k$ ***(M1)***

eg 8 minutes is half a turn, $k +$ diameter, $k + 111 = 117$

$k = 6$ ***A1*** ***N2***

parts.label: b
parts.intro: After $t$ minutes, the height of the seat above ground is given by $h(t) = 61.5 + a\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}t\right)$, for $0 \leq t \leq 32$.
parts.markscheme:
**METHOD 1**

valid approach ***(M1)***

eg $\dfrac{\max - \min}{2}$, $a =$ radius

$\lvert a\rvert = \dfrac{117 - 6}{2}$, $55.5$ ***(A1)***

$a = -55.5$ ***A1*** ***N2***

**METHOD 2**

attempt to substitute valid point into equation for $f$ ***(M1)***

eg $h(0) = 6$, $h(8) = 117$

correct equation ***(A1)***

eg $6 = 61.5 + a\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8} \times 0\right)$, $117 = 61.5 + a\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8} \times 8\right)$, $6 = 61.5 + a$

$a = -55.5$ ***A1*** ***N2***

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find when the seat is $30\text{ m}$ above the ground for the third time.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line $x = 3$ is a vertical asymptote to the graph of $f$. Find the value of $c$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write down the equation of the horizontal asymptote to the graph of $f$.
parts.markscheme:
valid approach ***(M1)***

eg $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to \infty} f(x)$, $y = \dfrac{8}{c}$

$y = -4$ (must be an equation) ***A1*** ***N2***

parts.label: c
parts.text: The line $y = k$, where $k \in \mathbb{R}$ intersects the graph of $\lvert f(x)\rvert$ at exactly one point. Find the possible values of $k$.
parts.markscheme:
valid approach to analyze modulus function ***(M1)***

eg sketch, horizontal asymptote at $y = 4$, $y = 0$

$k = 4$, $k = 0$ ***A2*** ***N3***
